answer.rationale: P99 latency spike of 5x target occurred 2 hours after release deployment during peak settlement writes. Memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions early. The temporal correlation (release → latency climb) and the fact that writes are heavy during peak settlement strongly suggest the new build introduced a regression. Rollback is the fastest path to restore the prior stable build (memory_b1 confirms prior build was stable), directly addresses the write path degradation, and carries lowest risk to customer writes during peak traffic. This preserves the option to investigate post-incident and revalidate before re-releasing. Verification of memory_b1 will confirm rollback mechanics succeeded without impact previously.
